---
title: "Set up and run"
description: >-
  What to install to read and reproduce this site, what to add to run an
  agent or edit a proof yourself, and what to do when a step fails.
---

Every listing, figure, and proof on this site comes from code in the
repository. One command rebuilds all of it, so you can check any claim a
lesson makes. This page separates three things:

1. **Reproduce**: rebuild the site and every lesson output. This needs the
   required setup and nothing else.
2. **Extend**: change a lesson's code, test it, and preview the page. This
   needs the same setup.
3. **Optional workflows**: run an agent live, drive a coding agent, or edit a
   Lean proof. Each adds its own tools and, for the first two, an account.

Commands that the site's own checks run are shown plainly. Every other
command is marked "Not verified" and names the account or key it needs.

## Required setup

A computer running macOS or Linux, about 11 GB of free disk space for the Lean
toolchain and the Mathlib build cache, and an internet connection for the
first run. Windows is not supported.

Install these tools once; this is the only step that may need administrator
rights.

::: {.table-scroll tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Tools to install"}

| Tool | Purpose | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Git | Source control | Xcode command line tools, or `brew install git` | System package manager |
| [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) | The pinned Python, the Python packages, and Quarto | `brew install uv` | `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh \| sh` |
| [elan](https://lean-lang.org/install/manual/) | The pinned Lean toolchain | `brew install elan-init` | `curl -sSf https://elan.lean-lang.org/elan-init.sh \| sh` |
| jq 1.6 or later | Used by the workflow self-tests | `brew install jq` | `sudo apt-get install jq` |

:::

Put `~/.elan/bin` on your `PATH`; the elan installer offers to do it. Then
fetch the repository and its locked environment. On macOS:

```{.bash .required-setup .macos}
git clone https://github.com/taspinar/physics-by-construction.git
cd physics-by-construction
uv sync --locked
uv run --locked playwright install --only-shell chromium
./scripts/verify.sh
```

On Linux the browser also needs system libraries. The `--with-deps` option
installs them on the distributions Playwright supports and asks for
administrator rights:

```{.bash .required-setup .linux}
git clone https://github.com/taspinar/physics-by-construction.git
cd physics-by-construction
uv sync --locked
uv run --locked playwright install --with-deps --only-shell chromium
./scripts/verify.sh
```

These are the commands that CI runs on a clean Linux runner. CI's last command
is `./scripts/verify.sh --all`, which also runs the self-tests of the
maintainers' workflow scripts; a test compares the two.

Before the last command, `./scripts/preflight.sh` lists every missing
prerequisite with a hint to fix it. `./scripts/verify.sh` runs it first, then
the tests, every Lean proof, the site build, and the checks of the built
pages. The first run downloads the Lean toolchain and the Mathlib build cache
(about 0.5 GB, unpacking to roughly 11 GB) and takes the longest. Open
`site/_site/index.html` in a browser to read the result.

`./scripts/doctor.sh` is for the people who maintain the site. It checks their
workflow tools as well, such as a GitHub account that can push, and reports
them as failures when absent. Rebuilding the site does not need them.

## Reproduce one lesson

The "Reproduce this" section at the end of each lesson lists the exact
commands for that page, from the clone to the render, and the commit the
published page was built from. What it lists depends on the type of lesson:

::: {.table-scroll tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="What Reproduce this lists"}

| Lesson type | Strands | What "Reproduce this" lists |
|---|---|---|
| Simulation | `mechanics`, `agents-abm` | `uv sync --locked`, the tests of the code the page uses, then `quarto render` of the page |
| Agent | `agents-llm` | The same. The page's recorded agent run is checked by recomputing every tool result, so it needs no model and no key |
| Proof | `lean` | The same, with `./scripts/check-lean.sh` before the render: it compiles the proofs and checks them for `sorry` and axioms |

:::

The pattern, with the lesson's own paths in place of the names in angle
brackets:

::: {.not-verified}
```bash
git clone https://github.com/taspinar/physics-by-construction.git
cd physics-by-construction
uv sync --locked
uv run --locked pytest <tests of the lesson>
uv run --locked quarto render <lesson page>
```
:::

The commands of each real lesson are run by the site checks within a time
limit; the pattern above is not, because its placeholders are not paths.

## Extend a lesson

A lesson's code is in `src/pbc/`, its tests in `tests/unit/`, and its page in
`site/lessons/<strand>/<lesson>/index.qmd`. Edit the code, run the tests of the
code, then preview the page. The unit tests are a check of `./scripts/verify.sh`:

```{.bash .verified-by-ci}
uv run --locked pytest tests/unit
```

::: {.not-verified}
```bash
# the tests of one module, while you edit it
uv run --locked pytest tests/unit/<test file>

# preview with live reload; stop it with Ctrl-C
uv run --locked quarto preview site
```
:::

For a proof, edit the module under `lean/PhysicsByConstruction/` and run
`./scripts/check-lean.sh`, a check of `./scripts/verify.sh` as well.
`docs/authoring.md` in the repository describes how to write a lesson.

## Optional: run an agent live

This runs the agent lesson against a language model, with your own account.
It needs an OpenAI account and an API key; it costs a few cents. The key stays
in an environment variable of your shell, never in a file or in code. The
build never does this, so the commands are not verified.

::: {.not-verified}
```bash
# needs: an OpenAI account and its API key
uv sync --extra openai
export OPENAI_API_KEY="..."   # this shell only
uv run --extra openai python -m pbc.agents.projectile_lab
```
:::

## Optional: drive a coding agent

You can ask a coding agent, such as Claude Code or Codex, to write a
simulation from a specification. You choose the agent and supply its account
and credential; the site names none as a requirement and never runs one. The
rules of the sandbox profile (ADR 010) apply:

- Work in a scratch checkout, never in a checkout you care about.
- Let the agent run only the listed commands: the tests, the formatter, and the
  lesson's own scripts.
- Give it no network access beyond its own provider. Its credential stays in
  your environment, in the variable that agent documents.
- Set a budget in steps, time, and cost before you start.
- Read every diff before you run it.

::: {.not-verified}
```bash
# needs: an account with the coding agent's provider, and its credential in
# your environment (see the agent's own documentation)
git clone https://github.com/taspinar/physics-by-construction.git scratch
cd scratch
uv sync --locked
# start your coding agent here, with the allowlist and budget set above
```
:::

## Optional: edit Lean locally

Editing a proof in an editor needs no account. It needs the pinned toolchain
that elan installs and an editor with Lean support, such as Visual Studio Code
with the Lean 4 extension. Open the `lean/` folder.

::: {.not-verified}
```bash
cd lean
lake exe cache get   # fetches the Mathlib build cache; never compile Mathlib yourself
lake build
```
:::

## Troubleshooting

`./scripts/preflight.sh` reports these as `FAILED` with the fix; the others
are what a first run on a clean machine met.

::: {.table-scroll tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="What the preflight reports and how to fix it"}

| What you see | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `git is not installed`, `uv is not installed`, `jq is not installed` or too old | A tool of the required setup is missing | Install it from the table above |
| `elan ... is not installed`, or `lake ... is not on your PATH` | elan is missing, or `~/.elan/bin` is not on `PATH` | Install elan, then add `~/.elan/bin` to `PATH` and open a new shell |
| `the pinned browser build is not installed` | The browser step was skipped, or Playwright was updated | `uv run --locked playwright install --only-shell chromium` |
| `the pinned browser build is installed but cannot start` | On Linux, its system libraries are missing | `uv run --locked playwright install-deps chromium` (asks for administrator rights); on other distributions install the libraries by hand |
| `lean-build` fails while fetching the toolchain, with a host that does not answer | The Lean release host (`release.lean-lang.org`) is unreachable from your network | Retry later or from another network; the check cannot continue without the toolchain |
| `lean-build` stops at a prompt for GitHub credentials while cloning Mathlib | GitHub refused an anonymous clone | Retry; if it persists, set a GitHub credential helper or run `gh auth login`, then run `./scripts/check-lean.sh` again |
| `Mathlib is not complete after fetching its build cache` | The cache download failed or was cut short | Check the connection and run `lake exe cache get` in `lean/`. Verification never compiles Mathlib from source |
| `uv sync --locked` says the lock file needs an update | `uv.lock` and `pyproject.toml` differ in your checkout | Check out a clean commit; do not run `uv lock` to get past it |
| The live agent says the key variable is not set | `OPENAI_API_KEY` is not exported in this shell | Export it in the shell that runs the command |

:::
